# md-first

> An experiment in serving a website as markdown. One HTML page exists, at `/`, for humans who arrive by link. Every other URL returns a `.md` file straight off disk with no HTML wrapper, no build step and no renderer in between.

Every link below returns `text/markdown; charset=utf-8` to any client that does not specifically ask for HTML. Appending `?raw` forces markdown for every client. The `.md` extension is optional: `/thesis` and `/thesis.md` return identical bytes.

## Start here

- [Thesis](/thesis.md): why HTML is the wrong default once the reader is a model, and what the counter-arguments are
- [How it works](/how-it-works.md): routing, content negotiation, and the response headers that make a markdown URL behave like a web page
- [The experiment](/experiment.md): the hypothesis, what is being measured, and the results that would kill it

## Conventions

- [Spec](/spec.md): the rules any md-first site follows, written so another site can copy them
- [Frontmatter](/docs/frontmatter.md): the YAML block that replaces `<head>`: title, description, canonical, updated
- [Discovery chain](/docs/discovery-chain.md): robots.txt to llms.txt to sitemap.xml to the .md files themselves
- [Content negotiation](/docs/content-negotiation.md): which clients render markdown inline, which download it, and why the Content-Type flips

## Build on it

- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart.md): clone, run, deploy, and convert an existing site
- [Live request log](/stats.md): generated markdown showing which clients have read this site and what they were served

## Optional

- [Full text](/llms-full.txt): every page on this site concatenated into one file
- [Sitemap](/sitemap.xml): the same URLs in XML, for crawlers that want it
